stories.headline: THE MACHINES Hold Off Master-Jeti
stories.dek: THE MACHINES 109.22, Master-Jeti 78.14. 7 lead changes, and the last one was the only one that kept.
paragraphs: They could not stop trading punches and I could not stop watching. THE MACHINES and Master-Jeti swapped the lead 7 times before one of them finally kept it, and THE MACHINES were the ones holding it when the weekend ran out: 109.22–78.14.

They took it in the second quarter — DJ Moore with an 11-yard touchdown catch, 55.78–52.9 — and then simply never gave it back. 10 touchdowns were scored after that and not one of them put Master-Jeti in front again.
THE MACHINES moved to 8-0, first in Spartan. Master-Jeti fell to 3-5 and fourth straight defeat, fourth in Spartan. THE MACHINES sit first in the league on the full table, 909 points scored.

Jaylen Warren led the winners with 20.3, backed by Puka Nacua and Trey McBride, who were not merely present. Braelon Allen actually outscored every man on the field with 21.3 and still lost, which tells you plenty about the other nine spots.
Master-Jeti started Tez Johnson and were rewarded with 0.0 points. That is a lineup slot that did nothing at all on Sunday.
Good teams win these without anybody noticing. That is the trick.

stories.headline: Killer Klowns Leave No Doubt
stories.dek: Killer Klowns 131.38, Lil’ Chops 90.84. 8 lead changes, and the last one was the only one that kept.
paragraphs: I lost track twice and I am paid to keep track. Killer Klowns beat Lil’ Chops 131.38 to 90.84, and the 40.5 points between them at the end flatter nobody — they traded the lead 8 times and then Lil’ Chops stopped trading.

They took it in the second quarter — Michael Wilson with a 17-yard run, 70.7–69.42 — and then simply never gave it back. 12 touchdowns were scored after that and not one of them put Lil’ Chops in front again.
Killer Klowns moved to 4-4, second in Spartan. Lil’ Chops fell to 4-4, third in Spartan.

Bhayshul Tuten did the heaviest lifting — a 39-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, the Sunday early games, worth 9.9 on its own. Bo Nix and Michael Wilson did the rest of the damage. Lil’ Chops got 23.0 from Bucky Irving and almost nothing from anybody standing near him.
Lil’ Chops left Emmett Johnson and his 20.3 on the bench and played Aaron Rodgers in the spot instead, for 1.4. Nobody will remember it, which is the kindest outcome available.
Next week is also a football game. That is the encouraging part.

stories.headline: Kupp Wins It Late for Smoke Dragons
stories.dek: Smoke Dragons 105.1, StillTheCream 97.74. 7.4 points in it.
paragraphs: Nobody could put this away, which is the polite version. Smoke Dragons were behind this football game until the fourth quarter and won it 105.1 to 97.74, which tells you most of what you need and none of how it felt.

The play that settled it came in the fourth quarter, Monday night: Cooper Kupp with a 7-yard touchdown catch. That put Smoke Dragons in front at 103.9–97.74, and for all the traffic that had come before it, nobody took it back. There were 10 touchdowns in this game and the one that mattered went Smoke Dragons’s way last.
Smoke Dragons moved to 3-5, fourth in Spectre Syndicate. StillTheCream fell to 4-4, first in Spectre Syndicate.

Tyler Allgeier did the heaviest lifting — a 63-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, the Sunday early games, worth 12.3 on its own. Kyler Murray and Chase McLaughlin did the rest of the damage. Jordan Love answered with 21.8 and it finished 7.4 short.
A few points the other way and we are writing a different piece.

stories.headline: Guido Haters Hold Off The Powers of Pain
stories.dek: Guido Haters 93.52, The Powers of Pain 73.5.
paragraphs: The sort of win you forget by Thursday and mention in December. Guido Haters 93.52, The Powers of Pain 73.5, a 20.0-point margin that never seriously came under review.

They took it in the first quarter — Ja'Marr Chase with a 30-yard touchdown catch, 37.7–34.2 — and then simply never gave it back. 9 touchdowns were scored after that and not one of them put The Powers of Pain in front again.
Guido Haters moved to 3-5 and a second straight win, third in Spectre Syndicate. The Powers of Pain fell to 3-5 and a second straight defeat, second in Spectre Syndicate.

Ja'Marr Chase did the heaviest lifting — a 30-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter, the Sunday early games, worth 9.0 on its own, though it was Kirk Cousins who finished with the biggest number at 29.2. Ja'Marr Chase and Josh Jacobs did the rest of the damage. Pittsburgh Steelers answered with 20.0 and it finished 20.0 short.
The Powers of Pain started Brock Purdy and were rewarded with 0.0 points. One of ten starting places, spent on nothing whatsoever.
That is the week. The next one starts immediately, as they do.

stories.headline: BIG BLUE Win the Last Exchange
stories.dek: BIG BLUE 127.56, Pork Chop Express 111.2. 6 lead changes, and the last one was the only one that kept.
paragraphs: Somebody please check on the men who had money on this. BIG BLUE and Pork Chop Express swapped the lead 6 times before one of them finally kept it, and BIG BLUE were the ones holding it when the weekend ran out: 127.56–111.2.

They took it in the second quarter — Joe Burrow with a 25-yard touchdown pass, 59.22–55.02 — and then simply never gave it back. 19 touchdowns were scored after that and not one of them put Pork Chop Express in front again.
BIG BLUE moved to 4-4 and a second straight win, third in Black and Blue. Pork Chop Express fell to 6-2, second in Black and Blue.
Joe Burrow led the winners with 40.2, and Tee Higgins and Malik Willis saw to the remainder. D'Andre Swift answered with 25.9 and it finished 16.4 short.
Pork Chop Express left Saquon Barkley and his 11.4 on the bench and played Michael Penix Jr. in the spot instead, for -4.4. It went unpunished, which is how habits form.
I aged a year on that one, and I was already old.

stories.headline: Wookie Leaks Hold Off Beaver Eaters
paragraphs: A game happened here. I was present for it. Wookie Leaks 110.38, Beaver Eaters 99.04, an 11.3-point margin that never seriously came under review.

They took it in the first quarter — Tony Pollard with a 40-yard touchdown run, 11.4–10.7 — and then simply never gave it back. 12 touchdowns were scored after that and not one of them put Beaver Eaters in front again.
Wookie Leaks moved to 3-5, fourth in Black and Blue. Beaver Eaters fell to 6-2 and a second straight defeat, first in Black and Blue.

Tony Pollard did the heaviest lifting — a 40-yard touchdown run in the first quarter, the Sunday early games, worth 10.0 on its own. Jonah Coleman and Washington Commanders did the rest of the damage. Jahmyr Gibbs answered with 22.8 and it finished 11.3 short.

Beaver Eaters will want to look away from this next bit. Adonai Mitchell sat on their bench and scored 20.2 while Marquise Brown held the same slot and returned 1.7 — 18.5 points in a chair, in a game they lost by 11.3. That is not a defeat, that is a self-inflicted wound with a witness.
Respectable, forgettable, and done.

stories.headline: Horsecollars Hang On
paragraphs: Close games are only fun when you are not in them. Horsecollars 83.24, n.W.o 80.0, a 3.2-point margin.

They took it in the first quarter — Savion Williams with an 18-yard run, 2.8–1.5 — and then simply never gave it back. 11 touchdowns were scored after that and not one of them put n.W.o in front again.

Horsecollars moved to 6-2 and a second straight win, first in The Four Horsemen. n.W.o fell to 2-6 and fourth straight defeat, third in The Four Horsemen. n.W.o are fifteenth of 16, and the 629 points scored is most of the reason — 174 short of the middle of the league.

Blake Corum did the heaviest lifting — a 23-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, the Sunday late games, worth 8.3 on its own, though it was Jacksonville Jaguars who finished with the biggest number at 20.0. Geno Smith and Blake Corum did the rest of the damage. Patrick Mahomes actually outscored every man on the field with 25.0 and still lost, which tells you plenty about the other nine spots.
That result will look very different in December.

stories.headline: Phins Phag Handle Gumbas
paragraphs: This had the shape of a competitive game without ever being one. Phins Phag 71.08, Gumbas 37.58, a 33.5-point margin that never seriously came under review.
There is no sequence to describe, because there was no sequence. Phins Phag scored first, kept scoring, and the remainder was arithmetic performed in public.

Phins Phag moved to 2-6, fourth in The Four Horsemen. Gumbas fell to 3-5, second in The Four Horsemen. Gumbas are fourteenth of 16, and the 557 points scored is most of the reason — 246 short of the middle of the league.
Cam Ward led the winners with 24.2, and Chuba Hubbard and Jordan Addison kept him company. Caleb Williams had 11.0 of it for Gumbas. The other nine spots have some explaining to do.
Phins Phag left DeMario Douglas and his 13.6 on the bench and played Omar Cooper Jr. in the spot instead, for 0.0. A free lesson, and those are the only ones anybody takes.
A win you can put in the bank and forget the account number.
